newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Arafat urges Islamic states to unite vs Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arafat urges Islamic states to unite vs Israel.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Tuesday called for an united stance by Islamic countries to prevent Israel from creating new Jewish settlements in east Jerusalem.

"It's a deliberate act from the Israeli government for Judaization of Jerusalem. The Islamic Ummah must take a united stance," Arafat was quoted by a Bangladesh foreign ministry official as saying at a meeting with Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in Dhaka.

"It's a violation of the Oslo agreement and the assurance given to us by the U.S.A," Bangladesh Foreign Secretary Farooq Sobhan, speaking at a news conference after the talks, further quoted the Palestinian leader as saying.
Arafat, South African President Nelson Mandela and Turkish President Suleyman Demirel arrived in Dhaka on Tuesday to attend celebrations of Bangladesh's 26th independence anniversary on Wednesday.
Hasina also held talks separately with Demirel and Mandela.
Before leaving Sri Lanka for Bangladesh earlier on Tuesday, Arafat said he was ready to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to discuss peace in the Middle East.
"Why not? If this is for peace I am ready, but if it is for propaganda, it is something different," Arafat told a news conference in the Sri Lankan capital Colombo.
Arafat accused Israel of fomenting confrontation between Palestinian groups, saying it wanted civil war.
The Palestinian President is scheduled to fly to Morroco from Dhaka late on Wednesday to attend a meeting of the Al Quds (Jerusalem) committee of the Organisation of Islamic Conference.
Bangladesh Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad is expected to travel with Arafat to the Rabat meeting, which is likely to discuss the latest crisis in Palestine, foreign ministry officials said.
Sobhan said Bangladesh and Turkey had signed two agreements, one on air transport, and the other on cultural and scientific cooperation during talks between Hasina and Demirel.
"We are expecting direct air links between Dhaka and Istanbul soon," Sobhan said.
He said Turkey had offered Bangladesh use of its free port for storage and transport of goods to central Asian and European markets.
Bangladesh proclaimed independence from Pakistan on March 26, 1971, and achieved it on December 16 the same year after a nine-month war in which it was helped by India.
Independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, father of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and the first president of Bangladesh, was assassinated with most of his family in a military coup in August 1975.
